title: Astoria  POC scoping: open-model shortlist & benchmarks
summary: Initial POC scoping to define success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan and shortlist open models. Customer prioritizes multilingual accuracy (EN/ES/FR), low hallucination for finance docs, and predictable latency under 250ms p95. Discussed tradeoffs between model quality and throughput, quantization options, and timeline for a 3-week pilot.
topics: Success criteria (latency, hallucination/error rate, cost per 1k tokens)
Workload sizing (QPS, concurrency, average tokens per call)
Benchmark plan and metrics (accuracy, hallucination, latency, cost)
Open-model shortlist and quality tradeoffs (Llama3, Mistral, Falcon, MPT)
Timeline and next steps for POC
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey team, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Maria - Astoria: Hi, Maria here, head of ML. we'll lead evals for this POC, focusing on finance doc summarization and question answering, and some Spanish support.
[00:15] Jae - Astoria: Jae, eng lead, will run benchmarks and infra.
[00:20] Noah - Astoria: Noah, product, here for success criteria.
[00:24] Priya - Astoria: Priya from security, I'll review compliance bits.
[00:28] Samir (SE): Great. quick agenda: success criteria, workload, shortlist, benchmarks, timeline.
[00:35] Alex (AE): High level  Astoria wants a 3-week POC, minimal infra lift, likely start hosted then move to dedicated if we need throughput or private networking. is that right?
[00:42] Maria: yes. key is accuracy on financial QAs and low hallucination. tolerable latency p95 ~250ms for single-turn QAs, batch summarize jobs can be higher.
[00:52] Jae: Our baseline is OpenAI GPT-4 in experiments, but cost is high. we're exploring open models to reduce unit cost. also need Spanish and French parity.
[01:05] Samir (SE): Understood. a couple clarifying Qs: what QPS and concurrency should we expect? average tokens per request?
[01:12] Maria: For interactive QA, about 10-20 QPS peak across global users, with 50 concurrent sessions. average request ~180 tokens in, 120 tokens out. for nightly summarization, we run bulk jobs of ~2000 documents, but that's async.
[01:28] Alex: ok that maps to a workload that can be served on modest dedicated capacity but fine on hosted during POC.
[01:34] Jae: SLA wise, if we go dedicated later, we need predictable tail latency  p95 under 250ms under sustained load.
[01:41] Samir: noted. on metrics  we'll measure latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and a hallucination/precision metric using your eval prompts. Maria, can you share a small eval set?
[01:52] Maria: yes, we'll share 200 labeled QA pairs in EN/ES/FR and 50 summarization golden references.
[01:58] Alex: perfect. now on model shortlist  common open models for this use are Llama 3 variants, Mistral 7B/Chat, Falcon 40B, MPT-30B, and smaller hybrids like OpenLlama or Llama 2 derivatives. we recommend testing 3 candidates with different quality/throughput profiles.
[02:18] Noah: what tradeoffs should we expect?
[02:21] Samir: short answer: bigger models usually give higher quality and fewer hallucinations but cost more and have higher latency. quantized 8-bit or 4-bit can reduce memory and cost but sometimes slightly hurts accuracy. for multilingual finance, models trained on diverse corpora (Mistral, Llama3) tend to perform better.
[02:40] Jae: any Redwood product name hiccups we should watch for? (laughs) like Redwood Dedikated?
[02:45] Alex: (laughing) yes some transcripts call it 'Redwood Dedikated' but it's Redwood Dedicated. also note our runtime does KV cache and prefix caching which helps conversational flows.
[02:56] Priya: on security, we need SOC2 type II and data handling  will you provide audit logs and KMS integration?
[03:03] Lina (SE): yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments and provide audit logs; for hosted POC we can enable customer-controlled retention and take a brief security questionnaire.
[03:13] Priya: also need data residency for EU users, can we pin region?
[03:17] Alex: yes EU region available for hosted, and dedicated/private supports customer VPC for full control.
[03:23] Samir: back to models  recommended POC shortlist: 1) Mistral-Instruct / Mistral 7B chat as a high throughput multilingual candidate, 2) Llama 3 13B (or a chat-optimized variant) as higher-quality mid-size, 3) Falcon 40B/chat or MPT-30B for a high-quality, larger-model baseline.
[03:43] Maria: curious about hallucination numbers  how will we measure?
[03:46] Samir: we'll run the labeled QA set and compute exact-match/conservative-precision, plus a hallucination rate defined as incorrect assertions per answer. we'll also run ROUGE/BERTScore for summarization against your golden refs.
[03:58] Jae: for throughput testing, can we run an end-to-end benchmark on Redwood Dedicated? we might need to reproduce our prod pattern (10-20 QPS, bursts to 50).
[04:06] Lina: yes, we can provision a short-lived dedicated pool for benchmark runs, or run on hosted with synthetic load. for heavy concurrency, dedicated gives more predictable p95.
[04:15] Noah: timeline  what are realistic dates?
[04:18] Alex: if eval data is shared by Friday (this week), Redwood can configure and run initial benchmarks within 5 business days; then 1 week of quality evals and tuning, so ~3 weeks end-to-end.
[04:30] Maria: that fits. cost expectations? we need a rough delta vs GPT-4 pricing to justify open models.
[04:36] Samir: we'll produce cost estimates per candidate model (tokens/sec, vCPU/GPU hours, quantization impact). expect 40-70% lower unit cost depending on model and quantization.
[04:47] Priya: about compliance documents  send SOC2 cert and data processing addendum.
[04:51] Alex: yep will include that in next steps.
[04:54] Speaker 1: (overlap) can you also include sample SDK snippets for our infra?
[04:58] Lina: we'll include SDK examples for streaming, function calling, and the inference client.
[05:04] Noah: one more  any limitations with multilingual tokenizers or rare-cases for Spanish legal text?
[05:09] Samir: some models have tokenization quirks  we'll surface any preprocessing needed. for legal/finance jargon we might need a short fine-tune or in-context prompt engineering; we'll test few-shot plus retrieval-augmented approaches in the POC.
[05:23] Maria: fine-tune may be a follow-up; for POC we just need to see baseline and whether hallucinations are acceptable.
[05:29] Alex: ok, recap and next steps coming from Redwood.
[05:33] Alex: action items  we'll run benchmarks on Mistral 7B chat, Llama3-13B chat, and Falcon 40B; produce cost comparison, latency profiles, and quality metrics on your eval set.
[05:45] Jae: we'll provide eval set and a sandbox account for testing by Thursday.
[05:50] Maria: schedule a mid-point check-in after initial benchmarks.
[05:53] Alex: great. thanks everyone.
[05:56] (call ends)
